s: Hi Georgie.
您好,乔治.
Phil
Hi Phil.
您好,菲尔.
Georgie
So, Georgie, do you often spend time with people who are much older than you or much younger than you?
乔治,你经常和比你年长或年轻的人在一起吗?
Phil
I do, actually, because I'm in a choir, so there's quite a wide range of ages – lots of older people, lots of younger people.
我确实是,因为我在合唱团,所以有很多年龄段,很多年长的人,很多年轻人.
Georgie
We can call an age group of people a generation .
我们可以称一个年龄组为一代.
Phil
And you might feel that it's difficult to understand or agree with people from a different generation .
你可能觉得很难理解或同意不同世代的人.

Today on 6 Minute English, we're going to be finding out about a project that is gathering together the oldest people – that's those that are retired – with the youngest, and that's children who attend nursery.
今天在6分钟英语节目上,我们将了解到一个项目,将年龄最大的人聚集在一起,
And we'll be asking the question, 'What can we learn from different generations ?'
我们会问",我们可以从不同世代中学到什么?"
Let's start with our quiz question, Georgie.
让我们从问题开始,乔治.
What generation would someone born in 1982 be in?
一个1982年出生的人属于哪一代?
Is it: a) Generation X, b) Millennial, or c) Gen Z.
是不是: (a) X代, (b) 千 ⁇ 一代,或者 (c) Z代.
Phil, I'm going to go with Generation X.
菲尔,我会选择X代.
Georgie
OK.
没有问题.
Phil
Well, we will find out the answer at the end of the programme.
我们将在课程结束时找到答案.
OK.
没有问题.
Georgie
Phil, so you said we're going to look at a project which gets small children interacting with older retired people.
菲尔,你说我们要看一个项目,让小孩子与老年人互动.
So, how does it work?
那么,它是如何工作的?
Well, in Chester, in the northwest of England, a nursery has opened up in a retirement village.
在英格兰西北部的切斯特, 一个养老村里开了一个幼儿园.
Phil
There's the usual nursery staff to look after the children, but the older residents can join in for activities as well.
常见的幼儿园工作人员照顾孩子,但老人也可以参加活动.

There's a library, a cafeteria and a garden for the children and the older people to share, and some of the older people or 'grand-friends', as the children call them, lead some of the activities, like dance or crafts.
有图书馆,餐厅和花园, 儿童和老年人可以分享, 有一些老年人或"大朋友",
And presenter of BBC World Service podcast People Fixing the World, Myra Anubi, went to visit the special nursery and spoke to some of the participants.
作为BBC世界服务播客播客主持人,
Ian was once a fighter pilot, and getting involved in the nursery has helped him fill a void .
伊恩曾经是战斗机飞行员, 参与幼儿园帮助他填补一个空白.
Myra Anubi
It was after my wife died last year.
这是我去年妻子去世后.
Ian
It seemed I had a big, big hole to fill.
我觉得我有个很大的空洞要填补.
And the people down in the nursery, they phoned me up and said, "We were doing such and such a thing.
孩子们在幼儿园里打电话给我说:"我们做了这样的东西.
Why don't you come and join us?"
你为什么不来和我们一起?"
And that's what I've been doing.
这就是我一直在做的事情.
So, yes, and I've enjoyed it.
所以,是的,我很享受.
And I find it very interesting to see how they develop.
我觉得很有趣看到它们的发展.
One of the things I heard from the grapevine is that you help the children make paper planes.
我从葡萄园听到的一件事是,你帮助孩子们制作纸机.
Myra Anubi
That's right.
这正是.
Ian
Myra says that the nursery helped Ian fill a void after his wife sadly died.
迈拉说,幼儿园帮助伊恩填补了妻子不幸去世后的空白.
Georgie
If you fill a void , you find something to help you feel better after a loss.
如果你填补了一个空白,你会找到一些帮助你失去后感觉更好的事情.
Ian explains that after his wife died, staff at the nursery would phone him to tell him about the daily activities, which he refers to as such and such .
伊恩解释说,妻子去世后,幼儿园的工作人员会打电话给他,
Phil
And that's an expression that we use to talk about something without giving a specific example.
这是一个我们使用的表达式来谈论某件事,而不给出具体的例子.
It sounds like Ian has enjoyed spending time with the children at the nursery, and Myra tells him she's heard from the grapevine that he's been teaching the children to make paper planes.
听起来伊恩很喜欢和孩子们在幼儿园度过时间, 迈拉告诉他她从葡萄园听说他一直在教孩子们制作纸机.
Georgie
Yes, hear from the grapevine is an expression, meaning that something is a rumour.
是的,从葡萄园听到的是一种表达式,意味着某事是谣言.
Phil
And we also say, hear on the grapevine .
我们还说,听从葡萄酒.
Well, this nursery sounds like a really lovely project, Phil.
这个幼儿园听起来很棒的项目,菲尔.
Georgie
What is the impact it's having on the older and younger people?
这对年长和年轻人产生了什么影响?

Well, the charity Ready Generations, which runs the nursery, says it works with universities to study the effects of mixing generations on health and wellbeing, and they say they've seen positive results.
现成一代的慈善机构, 经营幼儿园, 说它与大学合作研究混合一代对健康和幸福的影响,
Phil

And there have been studies around the world on projects that encourage different generations to mix, and they found that they can help reduce loneliness, improve how healthy and well people feel, and even boost learning and creativity.
世界各地都对鼓励不同世代混合的项目进行了研究,发现它们可以帮助减少孤独,改善人们的健康和健康感,甚至提高学习和创造力.
People Fixing the World host Myra spoke to Liz Ludden, co-founder of the nursery in Chester, about the differences that she's noticed since it opened.
人们修复世界的主持人迈拉和切斯特幼儿园的联合创始人丽兹·卢登谈到了自开放以来她注意到的差异.
And as I realised, these interactions also seem to be breaking down stereotypes .
我意识到,这些互动似乎也打破了刻板印象.
Myra Anubi
Your first thought would be how lively and energetic young children can be, and what we found is so can older people.
你的第一个想法是,小孩子有多活跃,有多充满活力,我们发现,
Liz Ludden
And so sometimes, you know, it's the older people that we're saying, "Can we just calm this down a little bit?"
所以有时,我们会问老年人, "我们可以安静一点吗?"
Myra says the nursery breaks down stereotypes .
迈拉说,幼儿园打破了刻板印象.
Georgie
This means it provides evidence that common beliefs about a group of people are not true.
这意味着它提供了证据表明人们对某个群体的普遍信仰是错误的.
For example, a stereotype about generations is that younger people are lively , meaning they're loud and have lots of energy, whereas older people are not that lively .
例如,关于一代人的刻板印象是年轻人活跃,这意味着他们很 ⁇ ,有很多能量,而年长人则不那么活跃.
Phil
Right.
现在,我们要去.
Georgie
But in the nursery, Liz says it's often the older people who have lots of energy and are being noisy rather than the children.
但在幼儿园里, 丽兹说,老年人经常有很多能量, 而不是孩子们.
The staff even have to tell them to calm down sometimes!
工作人员甚至有时会告诉他们要放松!
So, Georgie, is that something that you found in your choir?
所以,乔治,你在合唱团里发现了什么?
Phil
Actually, yes.
事实上,是的.
Georgie
The older people in my choir are big characters.
我合唱团中的老人是个大人物.
It's often them who are dragging us all to the pub...!
他们经常把我们带到酒吧!
OK.
没有问题.
Phil
Georgie, I think it's time to look at the answer for that question.
乔治,我认为是时候查看这个问题的答案.
I asked if someone was born in 1982, which generation would they be from?
我问,如果有人出生于1982年,他们来自哪一代?
I said Generation X.
我说X代.
Georgie
OK.
没有问题.
Phil
Well, actually, I'm afraid the answer was b) – they're a Millennial, just like you!
实际上,我害怕答案是b)  ⁇ 他们是千 ⁇ 一代,就像你一样!
啊!
Georgie
OK.
没有问题.
Let's recap the vocabulary we learned in this programme, starting with generation , which is a group of people who are of a similar age.
让我们回顾一下我们在这项课程中学到的词汇,
Fill a void means find something to help you feel better after experiencing loss.
填补一个空白意味着找到帮助你经历失去后感觉更好的事情.
Phil
Such and such is a way to talk about something without giving a specific example.
这种和这样的方法是谈论某事而没有给出具体的例子.
Georgie
If you hear something on the grapevine , you hear a rumour.
如果你在葡萄园听到什么,你会听到谣言.
Phil
The expression break down stereotypes means find evidence that common beliefs about a group of people are untrue.
"打破刻板印象"意味着找到证据表明人们对一群人的普遍信仰是错误的.
Georgie
And lively means loud and with lots of energy.
活跃的意思是大声,充满能量.
Phil
Once again, our six minutes are up, but you can test what you've learned with the worksheet on our website.
再一次,我们的六分钟已经过去了, 但你可以用我们网站上的工作表来测试你学到的东西.
Georgie
Go to bbclearningenglish.com.
进入 bbclearningenglish.com.
Thanks for joining us and goodbye.
谢谢你加入我们,再见.
Phil
Goodbye!
见面!
Georgie

w.hear: vt. 听到，倾听，听说；vi. 听见，听
w.lively: a. 活泼的，鲜明的，生动的
w.grapevine: n. 葡萄藤，葡萄树，秘密情报网
w.worksheet: [计] 工作表；[化] 工作单，加工单
w.rumour: n. 谣言，传闻；vt. 谣传
w.untrue: a. 不真实的，不正确的，不忠实的
w.stereotype: n. 铅版，陈规，老套；vt. 使用铅版，把...印制成盲文，套用老套
w.recap: vt. 翻新胎面；n. 翻新的轮胎
